Shader.description: A stage. One entry point per shader: a shader carrying both would emit the vertex module once per fragment stage that shares it.

Stream.description: ⚠ The contract between a vertex stage and the fragment stages that read it. A stream's location is its index in the declaration list, so adding one to a shader and not its partners moves every location after it — and what that produces is a stage reading the next value along. A stream a stage does not read is still declared, and costs no interface variable.

Bound resource.description: ⚠ A binding's index is its position among the shader's declarations, which is why a declared-and-never-read binding is sometimes load-bearing: leaving one out moves everything after it.

Push constant.description: ⚠ Raven emits a shader's whole block from offset zero and has no layout(offset =). A stage whose data the host writes at a non-zero offset has to declare that many bytes of padding first — see Vixen.Ui.Desktop's Ui.rvn, whose three compositing stages each carry a reserved: float4.

Range loop.description: ⚠ Ascending only. A walk that has to run the other way is written as a descending subscript over an ascending index.
